Guidance & outlook: Total Expenses decreased by 31.92% to INR 35,262.46 lakhs in FY26 from INR 51,792.59 lakhs in FY25.
Profit After Tax for FY26 stood at INR 1,156.25 lakhs as against INR 622.73 lakhs in FY25, representing a growth of 85.68%.
Profit After Tax for FY26 stood at INR 1,156.25 lakhs as against INR 622.73 lakhs in FY25, Le Merite Exports Limited Annual Report 2025-26 representing a growth of 85.68%.
Growth & demand: The global technical textile market reached $215.4 billion and is projected to expand to $335.8 billion by 2030, reflecting a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 6.5% to 7.2%.

PRECISION QUALITY CONTROL ARCHITECTURE • In-Line & final check Process Methodology • In-House Testing Laboratory • New Product Development (NPD) Focus STRATEGIC SYNTHESIS The convergence of explosive domestic market growth-guided by Indian government procurement mandates-and expanding international demand positions technical textiles as a high-margin growth …
Total Comprehensive Income also increased significantly to INR 1,158.13 lakhs from INR 619.81 lakhs in FY25, registering a growth of 86.85%.
Margins & costs: The global textile industry continued to operate in an environment influenced by changing consumer demand, input-cost movements, geopolitical developments, currency fluctuations and evolving international trade dynamics.
We continued to work towards improving productivity, optimising costs, enhancing manufacturing efficiencies and developing stronger customer relationships.

Cost Records & Audit Maintenance of cost records and requirement of cost audit as prescribed under the provisions of Section 148(1) of the Companies Act, 2013 are not applicable to the business activities carried out by the Company.
Capex & expansion: Our ongoing focus on modernisation, capacity enhancement and technological advancement is intended to position the Company to meet evolving customer requirements.
LMEL intends to actively participate in this evolving ecosystem by investing in capabilities, developing value-added products and leveraging relevant Government schemes and initiatives.

RAW MATERIAL MATRIX & BASE FORMULATIONS PROCESSING, FINISHING & COATING CAPABILITIES The greenfield plant processes diverse polymer compositions tailored to rigorous mechanical specifications: Nylon 6 & Nylon 6,6 (Polyamide): Engineered for ultra-high tensile strength, elongation recovery, cut-and-slash resistance, and ballistic integrity.
Balance sheet & cash: We are particularly encouraged by the progress of our projects and engagements associated with DRDO, which provide an opportunity to leverage our textile capabilities for specialised Defence requirements.
Dividend The Board of Directors has decided not to recommend any dividend for the financial year 2025-26 in order to conserve resources and strengthen the company's financial position.

Dividend Distribution Policy of the Company which is available on the website of the https://www.lemeriteexports.com/pdf/Dividend-Distribution- Policy.pdf Transfer to Reserve The Company has not transferred any amount to the Reserves for the year ended March 31, 2026.
Risks & challenges: During FY 2025-26, the industry continued to navigate changing consumer preferences, cautious retail demand, inventory adjustments, raw-material price volatility and geopolitical uncertainties.

GLOBAL DEMAND AND GEOPOLITICAL UNCERTAINTY Economic slowdowns, changing consumer demand, geopolitical tensions and evolving trade policies may affect export orders and international business conditions.

Staying one step ahead of risk The Company has laid down a well-defined risk management mechanism covering the risk mapping and trend analysis, risk exposure, potential impact, and risk mitigation process.
